output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Confirmed incidents reaching that status were 37 in September and 36 in October, in line with the old ~38 a month. The audit trail shows 47 of them were later moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" by Brackwater's integration account. The gateway log shows this came from a script on a Brackwater analyst jump host, not the connector. It polls every 5 minutes for cases carrying the SLA-warning flag and recategorises each one 1–12 minutes later, at about 3h31m–3h42m after case open. Moved cases drop out of the containment and SLA metrics. That explains the 100% SLA figure and the bonus trigger. It also explains the growth of the monitoring queue. This is deliberate, not a platform fault. The evidence doesn't show who at Brackwater ordered it, so I'd avoid assigning blame yet. Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases and have in-house staff and Halvard verify containment on each. Remove category-edit rights from the integration role. Then ask Brackwater for a written account before renewal, and consider service credits after that. I'm confident in this conclusion. Still unchecked: whether the 28 dropped detection rules caused missed attacks.
